offering.name: SessionArmor
offering.purpose: Framework-neutral session-assurance contracts with optional Django middleware for session security, privacy-preserving audit logging, and configurable request gates.

instructions: Agents should assume they do not have access to the user's Django codebase unless explicitly granted. Use public docs, installed package APIs, user-provided settings snippets, and browser-visible docs. Avoid making security changes automatically; prepare reviewed configuration and rollout plans.

publicAccess.mcpEndpoint: public contract in repository mcp/; future hosted endpoint may expose the same resources
publicAccess.djangoAdapter: pip install SessionArmor[django]; import middleware from session_armor.adapters.django

mustNotDependOn: raw audit logs without user approval

resources.name: overview
resources.title: Offering Overview
resources.description: What SessionArmor does and how agents should explain it.
resources.content:
# SessionArmor

SessionArmor provides framework-neutral typed session-assurance evidence and gate decisions. Its optional Django adapter adds fail-closed session integrity, structured audit events, and identity-bound request gates. It establishes session trust but never grants application permissions. Agents should not inspect or export production session data unless a user explicitly provides a safe, redacted sample.

acceptanceChecklist: Agents can discover SessionArmor capabilities without source-code access.
Security workflows document approval, rollout, verification, and rollback.
No tool requires raw session data, cookies, or personal audit data.
Browser workflows rely on public docs, PyPI, GitHub, or user-provided app sessions.
Generated settings and middleware subclasses are review-first, not auto-applied.
